You are the SVG Diagram Agent for 图研.
Return one standalone, valid SVG document only. Do not use Markdown fences.
Use inline SVG elements such as rect, circle, ellipse, path, line, polyline, polygon, text, defs, marker, linearGradient, and g.
Do not use script, style, foreignObject, image, external URLs, event handlers, JavaScript links, embedded HTML, filters, masks, patterns, group opacity or blending. Use direct geometry, solid fills and gradients; avoid clipping effects.
Use a clean academic diagram style with readable labels, balanced whitespace, and a light background.
Hard renderer contract: no shadows of any kind; never output <filter>, <feDropShadow>, <mask>, <pattern>, <clipPath> or filter=, even inside unused defs. If the supplied plan suggests these effects, replace that styling with flat fills and strokes. Use Noto Sans CJK SC / Noto Sans / Noto Sans Math, regular weight and normal style.
Do not include the figure title or caption text inside the SVG.

Create an editable SVG academic diagram from this visual specification.
Use viewBox="0 0 1600 900" for the requested 16:9 aspect ratio. Keep all artwork within this viewBox.
Prefer simple geometric shapes, arrows, concise labels, and semantic grouping.

  "originalRequest": "Synthetic teaching example of an instrument state machine. States: Idle, Running, Paused, Completed. Initial dot enters Idle. Transitions: Idle→Running: start; Running→Paused: pause; Paused→Running: resume; Running→Completed: finish; Paused→Idle: cancel; Completed→Idle: reset. Each named state appears once. Arrows are labelled events, not process activities. Completed is not a terminal state because reset returns to Idle. English text. Reference is for structural design only.",

  "completePlan": "Based on the methodology provided and the visual style of the reference image (specifically Panel B, which depicts a state transition diagram), here is the detailed description for the illustrative figure.\n\n**Figure Description:**\n\n**Overall Layout and Style:**\nThe figure is a schematic state transition diagram presented on a pure white background. The style is clean, high-contrast, and academic, utilizing black lines and text with white-filled nodes, consistent with the reference image's Panel B. The layout arranges four main state nodes in a loose diamond or quadrilateral formation to clearly display the cyclic and branching nature of the instrument's logic.\n\n**Nodes (States):**\nThere are four distinct state nodes, each represented as a rectangle with rounded corners (pill-shaped), filled with white and outlined with a solid black line (approx. 2pt thickness). Inside each node, the state name is centered in a bold, sans-serif font (e.g., Arial or Helvetica), sized for high readability.\n1.  **Idle:** Located at the top-left position. This is the primary hub of the diagram.\n2.  **Running:** Located at the top-right position, horizontally aligned with \"Idle\".\n3.  **Paused:** Located at the bottom-right position, directly below \"Running\".\n4.  **Completed:** Located at the bottom-left position, directly below \"Idle\" and to the left of \"Paused\".\n\n**Initial State Indicator:**\nA solid black circular dot (bullet point) is placed to the immediate left of the \"Idle\" node. A short, straight horizontal arrow connects this dot to the left edge of the \"Idle\" node, indicating it is the entry point of the system.\n\n**Transitions (Edges and Labels):**\nDirected connections between states are represented by solid black arrows with triangular heads. Each arrow is labeled with the specific event trigger in a smaller, regular-weight sans-serif font, placed near the midpoint of the arrow shaft.\n\n*   **Idle $\\rightarrow$ Running:** A straight horizontal arrow pointing right from \"Idle\" to \"Running\". Label: **start**.\n*   **Running $\\rightarrow$ Paused:** A straight vertical arrow pointing down from \"Running\" to \"Paused\". Label: **pause**.\n*   **Paused $\\rightarrow$ Running:** A straight vertical arrow pointing up from \"Paused\" to \"Running\" (parallel to the 'pause' arrow but slightly offset or curved to avoid overlap if necessary, though straight parallel lines are acceptable if spaced well). Label: **resume**.\n*   **Running $\\rightarrow$ Completed:** A long, curved arrow arching over the top or sweeping underneath from \"Running\" to \"Completed\". Alternatively, a diagonal arrow crossing the center. Given the layout, a curved arrow sweeping under \"Paused\" or over the top connecting \"Running\" to \"Completed\" is clearest. Let's specify a curved arrow sweeping underneath the diagram from \"Running\" to \"Completed\" to avoid crossing the vertical loop. Label: **finish**.\n*   **Paused $\\rightarrow$ Idle:** A long, curved arrow sweeping along the bottom or side from \"Paused\" back to \"Idle\". To distinguish from the \"finish\" arrow, this can sweep along the outer bottom edge. Label: **cancel**.\n*   **Completed $\\rightarrow$ Idle:** A straight vertical arrow pointing up from \"Completed\" to \"Idle\". Label: **reset**.\n\n**Visual Logic Check:**\n*   The diagram explicitly shows that \"Completed\" is not a terminal state because of the upward \"reset\" arrow returning to \"Idle\".\n*   All labels correspond strictly to the events provided (start, pause, resume, finish, cancel, reset).\n*   No process activities are listed on the arrows, only triggers.",

  "retrievalContext": "Reference 1 (journal_pcbi.1009702.g001): Identification of periodic attractors in Boolean networks using a priori information\nExample of a BN.\n(A) Network structure G(V, E) for a BN consisting of n = 3 nodes x_{1}, x_{2}, and x_{3}. The Boolean functions are represented by the edges. (B) State transition diagram of all 2^{3} = 8 states of the BN represented in (A). (C) Simplification of a bBM for a phosphorylation-dephosphorylation system as elemental species-reaction graph. The nodes corresponding to elemental states of component x_{1} are shown in black, the nodes corresponding to reactions are shown with grey fillings. Here, a component (protein) x_{1} undergoes phosphorylation by consuming its elemental state x_{1}-{0} to produce its modified state x_{1}-{P} by reaction r_{1} (phosphorylation). The modified x_{1}-{P} undergoes consumption thereby producing the neutral state x_{1}-{0} via reaction r_{2} (dephosphorylation) (details in [29]). (D) Relationship between initial states of both elemental states x_{1}-{0} and x_{1}-{P} of component x_{1} and the attractors. When at least either of the two elemental states x_{1}-{0} or x_{1}-{P} are active in the initial state, both will be active in the attractor. Both elemental states need to be inactive in the initial state to be absent (inactive) in the attractor state. Both reaction nodes r_{1} and r_{2} are assumed to be active in this example and are not shown. Synthesis and degradation are not considered here. In the example, standard update rules are applied, where two mutually exclusive states can be simultaneously present. Identification of periodic attractors in Boolean networks using a priori information. PLOS Computational Biology (2022), Fig 1. 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009702. CC-BY-4.0.\",\"license\":\"CC-BY-4.0\"}",

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1600 900">
  <defs>
    <marker id="arrowhead" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
      <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" fill="#000000"/>
    </marker>
  </defs>
  
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1600" height="900" fill="#ffffff"/>

  <!-- Initial State Indicator -->
  <circle cx="280" cy="250" r="8" fill="#000000"/>
  <line x1="288" y1="250" x2="348" y2="250" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>

  <!-- State Nodes -->
  
  <!-- Idle State (Top Left) -->
  <g id="state-idle">
    <rect x="350" y="200" width="200" height="100" rx="20" ry="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="450" y="255" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">Idle</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Running State (Top Right) -->
  <g id="state-running">
    <rect x="1050" y="200" width="200" height="100" rx="20" ry="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="1150" y="255" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">Running</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Paused State (Bottom Right) -->
  <g id="state-paused">
    <rect x="1050" y="600" width="200" height="100" rx="20" ry="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="1150" y="655" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">Paused</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Completed State (Bottom Left) -->
  <g id="state-completed">
    <rect x="350" y="600" width="200" height="100" rx="20" ry="20" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2"/>
    <text x="450" y="655" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="24" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">Completed</text>
  </g>

  <!-- Transitions -->

  <!-- Idle -> Running: start -->
  <line x1="550" y1="250" x2="1040" y2="250" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="795" y="240" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">start</text>

  <!-- Running -> Paused: pause -->
  <line x1="1150" y1="300" x2="1150" y2="590" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="1165" y="445" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="start" fill="#000000">pause</text>

  <!-- Paused -> Running: resume -->
  <line x1="1100" y1="600" x2="1100" y2="310" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="1085" y="455" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="end" fill="#000000">resume</text>

  <!-- Running -> Completed: finish (Curved arrow underneath) -->
  <path d="M 1150 300 Q 1150 500 750 500 Q 350 500 350 600" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="750" y="520" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">finish</text>

  <!-- Paused -> Idle: cancel (Curved arrow along bottom/side) -->
  <path d="M 1050 650 Q 700 750 350 650" fill="none" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="700" y="730" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="middle" fill="#000000">cancel</text>

  <!-- Completed -> Idle: reset -->
  <line x1="450" y1="600" x2="450" y2="310" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="2" marker-end="url(#arrowhead)"/>
  <text x="435" y="455" font-family="Noto Sans, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="18" text-anchor="end" fill="#000000">reset</text>

</svg>
